predecessors.name: Pandya dynasty
predecessors.text: Venadu, the southern Kerala part of Cliopatria's Pandya shape of 592-824 (the Pandya dossier's own reading of 'the liberation of Venadu from Pandya control')

predecessors.name: Chera Perumal kingdom
predecessors.text: Venad from Kollam in the north to Suchindram or Nagercoil in the south, including Nanjinadu (the Venadu page)

successors.name: Travancore
successors.text: Venad as Travancore inherited it, from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi in the south ('a small chiefdom extending from Edava in the north to Aralvaimozhi under the Venadu Kingdom', Marthanda Varma…

ledger.x: 825: Venadu is free of the Pandyas.
1005: Rajaraja I's Senur inscription lists Kollam.

c. 1124: Venad takes over southern Kerala as the Chera state ends. 'In southern Kerala, the medieval Chera dynasty was succeeded by the rulers of Venad (centered on the port of Kollam)'; 'In the early 12th century, the medieval Chera kingdom of Kerala dissolved into several local powers'. The…

c. 1275: the Pandyas take Kollam. 'In the latter half of the 13th century, Venadu came under the control of the Pandyas'; Maravarman Kulasekhara is 'the one who destroyed the Chera ruler and captured Kollam' (c. 1275 CE); Venadu 'likely became one of the Pandya state's mandalams'. The Ravi Varma Kulasekhara page calls…
1312: south Kerala slips out of Pandya hands.
1312: Ravivarman raids and crowns himself in the Pandya country.
early 14th century (bridged to 1317): the Kollam branch forms.
1729: Marthanda Varma succeeds to Venad and builds Travancore.

wars.name: Chola conquest of Kerala under Rajaraja I
wars.outcome: Chola victory: Rajaraja I's Senur inscription of 1005 lists the defeat of the rulers of Kollam (Venad).

wars.name: Pandya conquest of Kollam
wars.outcome: Pandya victory: Maravarman Kulasekhara captured Kollam and Venadu came under Pandya control for the rest of the 13th century.

wars.name: Ravivarman's raids on the Pandya country
wars.outcome: Short-lived Venad supremacy from Cape Comorin to Nellore, lost when the Kakatiya army took Kanchi (March-June 1316) and Ravivarman withdrew to Venad.

certainty.note: The pages name ports, districts and capitals, never a boundary; the Pandya, Chola and Chera frontiers in the south are approximate in every period.

sources.title: Chera Perumals of Kerala (Chera Perumals of Makkotai)
